LESSON: WRITING 14.5.1 DESCRIPTIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.5: Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What makes a story creative?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use the correct writing process to write a composition
2. spell words correctly in composition writing
3. apply the five senses in writing descriptive compositions
4. recognise the importance of creativity in writing

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 14.5.1 DESCRIPTIVE WRITING
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 14.5.1 DESCRIPTIVE WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Use the correct writing process to write a composition

What this means
In this part you learn to use the correct writing process to write a composition. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use the correct writing process to write a composition.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use the correct writing process to write a composition. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Spell words correctly in composition writing

What this means
In this part you learn to spell words correctly in composition writing. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: spell words correctly in composition writing.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can spell words correctly in composition writing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Apply the five senses in writing descriptive compositions

What this means
In this part you learn to apply the five senses in writing descriptive compositions. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply the five senses in writing descriptive compositions.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply the five senses in writing descriptive compositions. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Recognise the importance of creativity in writing

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise the importance of creativity in writing. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise the importance of creativity in writing.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise the importance of creativity in writing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use the correct writing process to write a composition)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing to a partner. (skill: spell words correctly in composition writing)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: apply the five senses in writing descriptive compositions)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: recognise the importance of creativity in writing)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use the correct writing process to write a composition.
3. Practise this skill: spell words correctly in composition writing.
4. Practise this skill: apply the five senses in writing descriptive compositions.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What makes a story creative?
2. Which words do we use to describe our different senses?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 14.5.1 Descriptive writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use the correct writing process to write a composition.
5. Be able to: spell words correctly in composition writing.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
